description: Return the 1-based sequence term consisting of 1 followed by integers n>1 with exactly eight positive divisors.

source.title: Numbers which are the cube roots of the product of their proper divisors
source.numeric_crosscheck_note: The linked translation labels the 500th, 5000th, and 50000th terms and reports 2526, 23118, and 223735, respectively.
source.algorithm_attribution: Enumerate the distinct prime signatures 7, 3+1, and 1+1+1 for tau(n)=8, then select the indexed value by binary search over value bounds.
source.implementation_status: Bounded clean-room indexed sequence profile; no upstream code copied

output.meaning: a(1)=1; for k>1, a(k) is the (k-1)th increasing integer n>1 with tau(n)=8

contract.definition: For n>1, n is the cube root of the product of its positive proper divisors iff tau(n)=8; the empty proper-divisor product makes n=1 the special first term.
contract.primary_method: Build a prime-count prefix table to 600000. Count numbers <=x by disjoint prime signatures p^7, p^3*q with p!=q, and p*q*r with pairwise distinct primes; binary-search the smallest x whose count reaches k-1.
contract.independent_method: Sieve tau(n) for all n<=600000 by incrementing every multiple for each divisor; scan the tau=8 positions to select k-1.
contract.invalid_cases: Null input, empty or trailing-word frame, k<1, or k>50000 returns -1.
contract.prime_signature_partition: If tau(n)=8, the exponent-plus-one factors are 8, 4*2, or 2*2*2, giving p^7, p^3*q, or p*q*r with distinct primes as encoded by each signature.
contract.binary_search_invariant: The searched predicate count_tau8(x)>=k-1 is monotone; the lower-bound search returns the first integer attaining it.
contract.overflow_proof: All values, prime powers, and products are bounded by 600000 using division guards before multiplication. The prime-prefix table entries and signature counts are at most 600000, so uint32 counters are sufficient. k and returned terms fit signed 64-bit values.
contract.maximum_term_evidence: The published task translation reports the 50000th term as 223735, below the conservative contract cap 600000. It also reports the 500th term as 2526 and the 5000th term as 23118; all three checkpoints are pinned in the workload.
contract.baseline_and_stretch: The task displays the first 50 terms, reports the 500th and 5000th terms, and includes a 50000th-term stretch checkpoint. The benchmark domain includes that bounded stretch target.

complexity.primary_time: O(B log log B + log B * B^(5/6)) for B=600000; the first term builds the prime-prefix table and each binary-search count enumerates bounded distinct-prime signatures.
complexity.primary_space: 600001 uint32 prime-prefix entries use 2400004 bytes; at most 124 additional bytes are budgeted for scalar loop, search, and argument state, for a 2400128-byte total cap. No quotient array is stored.
complexity.independent_time: O(B log B) divisor-count sieve and O(B) scan for B=600000.
